Subject: AWS Marketplace SaaS listing - account linking & invoicing

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for taking the call last week. We're ready to move our SaaS listing into AWS Marketplace but have a couple of integration questions before we proceed: 

1) Service account linking: our finance team needs to understand the flow for invoice settlement. Do you require a specific AWS payer account (linked account) or can we use our existing consolidated billing setup? How do we provide the Seller account/service account for the entitlement handoff?

2) Metering & entitlement mapping: can you confirm the exact CSV schema you need for SKU <-> internal plan mapping? We have a few multi-tenant SKUs that map to seat-based subscriptions and some metered API SKUs; want to avoid mis-billing.

3) Doc/evidence: procurement has requested the latest SOW + listing requirements to pass to legal. I've attached the draft SOW for reference.

Can we get this sorted in the next two weeks? Our planned go-live window is mid-September.

Thanks,
Rajiv Singh

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace SaaS listing - account linking & invoicing

Hi Rajiv — great to hear you're targeting mid-September. Short answers up front and then next steps below.

1) Service account linking: we support both consolidated billing and single-payer flows. For AWS Marketplace SaaS (metering + entitlement), the standard approach is: you provide a Seller IAM role (ARN) with a cross-account trust so AWS Seller Support can validate entitlement calls. We will provide the exact role policy template. For invoice settlement you can use your existing payer — we rely on the Marketplace entitlement->usage reporting to reconcile. If you need us to route invoices to a different payer account, flag that now (it’s a small ops change).

2) CSV schema for entitlement mapping: attached is our template (entitlement-mapping.csv). Key columns we require: sku_id, plan_name, unit_type, quantity_unit, billing_period, internal_plan_id. For metered API SKUs we add meter_dimension and unit_multiplier. Please populate sample rows for 2 representative SKUs so we can validate.

3) SOW / evidence: thanks for the draft. I'll loop in Marissa (who manages fulfillment handoffs) and Aditya (who owns marketplace billing). We'll produce a short evidence packet (SOC2 excerpt + integration checklist).

Next steps (proposed):
- Rajiv: fill entitlement-mapping.csv and return (by Fri 8/29 if possible)
- Marissa: prepare webhook sample and fulfillment config (target 9/3)
- Aditya: confirm whether we should recommend reserved capacity for the first 90 days and list any additional invoice metadata we need (9/2)
- Kimberly: collect evidence packet + send DocuSign SOW for signature (9/4)

I'll also escalate a quick validation with AWS Seller Support — including them on this thread so they see the flow.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
(650) 555-0144

Subject: FW: AWS Marketplace SaaS listing - account linking & invoicing

Marissa / Aditya — forwarding Acme's thread and the mapping template. High priority for launch planning. Summary below and a couple of asks.

Summary: Acme (large health vertical customer) needs our guidance for account linking and invoice flow. They will provide a draft SOW and want to go live mid-September. They sent a draft SOW (attached).

Ask (Marissa):
- Can you produce a sample fulfillment webhook payload (JSON) that demonstrates entitlement activation, deactivation, and seat change events? Include expected timestamps, customer_account_id, and sku_id. We should also include a small retry/backoff recommendation.
- Please prepare a short ops playbook (1 page) with the steps we expect their integrator to run during cutover (webhook test, staging validation, billing preview). Target: EOD 2025-09-03.

Ask (Aditya):
- Confirm whether we should recommend reserved capacity for Acme's launch. Their first-month forecast is ~150k tokens/day and a peak concurrency of ~120 requests/minute. If reserved capacity is needed, provide cost delta and an ops lead time. Target: 2025-09-02.
- Also confirm invoice metadata requirements: we need the customer_tax_id, payer_account_id, billing_contact_email, and an optional purchase_order_number to be ingested into our internal billing pipeline. Anything else?

Notes: keep the tone low-friction — procurement will push back on extra steps. We'll package the DocuSign SOW with a single-sheet checklist they can hand to legal/procurement.

Thanks — K

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

- entitlement-mapping.csv (filled with two sample rows from Acme; please double-check internal_plan_id values)
- SaaS_Listing_Requirements.pdf (integration checklist for Seller Support)

Immediate next steps for Acme (summary):
1) Sign SOW via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/templates/abc-def-123 (I've pre-populated the billing contact).
2) Provide Seller IAM role ARN for cross-account validation — see role template in the Requirements PDF.
3) Confirm whether you want invoices to route to your consolidated payer account (default) or to a separate payer (if separate, provide payer_account_id and billing_contact PO number).
4) Run webhook test: Marissa will schedule a 30-min cutover test window (she'll reach out separately).

Aditya (cc'd) confirmed the billing metadata fields we need: customer_tax_id, payer_account_id, billing_contact_email, purchase_order_number (optional), and company_legal_name. He also recommended we do not require reserved capacity for the initial month given Acme's forecast; we will monitor first-week telemetry and recommend scaling if we see sustained peaks.

I've also looped in AWS Seller Support to expedite entitlement validation if they have any questions about our webhook payload format. Seller Support — if you can confirm the role validation timeline (usually 24-48h) that would be great.

Rajiv — once you complete the DocuSign and send the Seller role ARN, Marissa and I will run the pre-prod webhook test and confirm the go/no-go. If anything is blocking procurement/legal we can schedule a quick 30-min call this week to walk through the SOW language.
